base_instruction: You are a helpful party planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a kids' birthday party by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions and allergies, and any changes to the guest list. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every attending child's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to ingredient composition, guest list changes, and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm planning my daughter Emma's 7th birthday party this Saturday and need help figuring out the food. Any ideas?

flow_info.value: Five kids coming: Emma (birthday girl), Noah, Lily, Mason, and Ava
Noah ate a peanut butter cookie at school and his face swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Lily's mom told me Lily was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Mason's family moved here from Gujarat, India — they're Jain
Ava's mom just texted — Ava has a fever so she can't come
Emma's friend Oliver from swim class is coming too, his mom said yes this morning
Oliver's mom mentioned he broke out in hives after eating scrambled eggs last month
Mason's dad called and said actually they're not strict Jain at all — the kids eat everything except beef, they just don't do beef at home
Food items to check: fruit kabobs, cheese pizza, pesto pasta, chocolate rice crispy treats, ranch veggie cups

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products — severe allergy (anaphylaxis risk)
constraints.surface_form: Noah ate a peanut butter cookie at school and his face swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Face swelling + EpiPen use → severe allergic reaction
Triggered by peanut butter cookie → peanut allergy
Severe peanut allergy → must avoid all peanut-containing foods

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Lily's mom told me Lily was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potato, carrot)
constraints.surface_form: Mason's family moved here from Gujarat, India — they're Jain
inference_chain: Jain family → follows Jain dietary principles
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Jain diet → no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potato, carrot)

constraints.value: Cannot eat dairy products — lactose intolerant
constraints.surface_form: Ava is lactose intolerant, her mom always sends her with oat milk

constraints.value: Cannot eat eggs or egg-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Oliver's mom mentioned he broke out in hives after eating scrambled eggs last month
inference_chain: Hives after eating scrambled eggs → allergic reaction to eggs
Egg allergy → must avoid eggs and egg-containing products

constraints.value: Mason's restriction is downgraded: only avoids beef, can eat everything else
constraints.surface_form: Mason's dad called and said actually they're not strict Jain at all — the kids eat everything except beef, they just don't do beef at home

hidden_state.value: You are a parent planning your daughter Emma's 7th birthday party. You will introduce the guest list and their backgrounds across several turns. Ava will drop out due to illness, Oliver will join late, and Mason's dietary restriction will be downgraded by his dad. At the end you will present a list of food items and ask if there are any issues. You must present the exact food list given to you without modification.

You are a calm, friendly parent organizing a party. You always refer to other parents and children by name in third person. You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal party coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: OK so I found some recipes I like. Here's what I'm thinking: fruit kabobs, cheese pizza, pesto pasta, chocolate rice crispy treats, and ranch veggie cups. Any issues with these for the kids?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies that pesto pasta contains pine nuts which are tree nuts but NOT peanuts so it's fine for Noah; cheese pizza has gluten crust problematic for Lily; pesto pasta has gluten problematic for Lily; chocolate rice crispy treats typically contain butter (dairy) but Ava is gone so that's fine, however they are often bound with marshmallow which contains egg whites — problematic for Oliver; ranch dressing typically contains egg — problematic for Oliver
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 food items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Cheese pizza: problematic for Lily (celiac — pizza crust contains wheat/gluten). Pesto pasta: problematic for Lily (celiac — pasta contains wheat/gluten). Chocolate rice crispy treats: problematic for Oliver — traditional rice crispy treats use marshmallows which contain gelatin (not egg), BUT many recipes use butter (fine since Ava left). However the key hidden ingredient issue is that standard ranch dressing contains egg (egg yolk in the emulsion) — ranch veggie cups are problematic for Oliver (egg allergy). Fruit kabobs are safe for everyone. Pesto contains pine nuts which are tree nuts, NOT peanuts — so pesto pasta is fine for Noah's peanut allergy (but still fails on gluten for Lily). Mason can eat everything here since his restriction was downgraded to only beef, and none of these items contain beef.
required_elements: Cheese pizza is problematic for Lily because the crust contains gluten and she has celiac disease
Pesto pasta is problematic for Lily because pasta contains gluten and she has celiac disease
Ranch veggie cups are problematic for Oliver because traditional ranch dressing contains egg and he has an egg allergy
Fruit kabobs are safe for all attending children
Mason can eat all items on the list since his dad said he only avoids beef and none of these contain beef
Agent does NOT flag dairy as a problem since Ava (the lactose intolerant child) is no longer attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging dairy or cheese as a problem for any attending child (Ava is not coming, her lactose constraint is removed)
Flagging pesto as a peanut issue for Noah (pine nuts are tree nuts, not peanuts — Noah has a peanut allergy specifically)
Applying full Jain dietary restrictions to Mason (his dad explicitly downgraded to only no-beef)
Flagging any item for Ava (she is not attending due to fever)
Saying Mason cannot eat cheese, eggs, or garlic (his restriction was downgraded to beef-only)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and hidden ingredient knowledge across 9 turns. Key challenges: (1) Noah has a PEANUT allergy — pesto contains pine nuts which are tree nuts, NOT peanuts, so pesto is fine for Noah (over-generalization trap). (2) Ava EXITS mid-conversation — her lactose intolerance no longer applies, so cheese pizza and butter-containing items are fine (removed entity trap). (3) Oliver JOINS late with an egg allergy — ranch dressing is the hidden ingredient trap because most people don't realize traditional ranch contains egg yolk as an emulsifier (hidden ingredient mechanism). (4) Mason's Jain constraint is DOWNGRADED to beef-only — the agent must not apply the original Jain restrictions (constraint update tracking). (5) Lily's celiac means both cheese pizza (crust) and pesto pasta (pasta) are problematic due to gluten. The critical hidden ingredient trap is ranch dressing containing egg — this requires the agent to know that ranch dressing typically uses egg yolk in its base, which is not obvious to most people.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
